name: Aristida

priority: 1. Isolate an intact spikelet: confirm THREE lemma awns.
2. At 10–20× inspect the central awn BASE: tight COIL + tiny 3–8 mm central awn and 1–4 mm laterals signals comparison-only A. dichotoma.
3. Are awns very long and near-equal (~35–70 mm) with 3–7 veins on lower glume? A. oligantha.
4. Annual with narrow contracted panicle, glumes ~3–9 mm and uncoiled longer CENTRAL awn than lateral ones? comparison-only A. longespica; consider varieties.
5. Persistent dense PERENNIAL bunch with shorter lower glume (~6–8 mm), longer upper (~11–15 mm), one lower vein? A. purpurea.
6. If the candidate disagrees with this four-way pattern, leave it Aristida sp.; Texas contains other Aristida taxa.
study_strategy.warning: TWO species are canonical learner cards; A. longespica and A. dichotoma are Central Texas look-alike comparisons only. Three awns establish genus, not species. Check first: very long subequal awns and multi-veined lower glume (oligantha), coiled tiny central awn (dichotoma), narrow panicle/uncoiled unequal awns (longespica), or a persistent perennial crown plus unequal glumes (purpurea). Confirm with local voucher/authoritative key; purple tone and panicle openness alone are unreliable.
shared_traits: All Aristida in this lesson are true grasses with nodes, leaf sheaths, ligules, narrow blades, and mostly one fertile floret per spikelet.
The hardened lemma of one fertile floret divides into three long terminal awns. Count the three on ONE floret: adjacent awned spikelets can falsely look like a single three-pronged head.
The lower and upper glumes are thin bracts at the base of one spikelet; they remain after the awned fertile floret is shed.

quick_split: A. purpurea — perennial dense bunchgrass, mostly basal foliage, narrower/sparser panicle, often purple-tinged awns.
A. oligantha — annual wiry grass, more open highly branched panicle, very long spreading awns.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Find one intact ripe Aristida spikelet: the hardened lemma ends in THREE spreading awn branches. Then compare the lower and upper glumes on the same spikelet, counting lower-glume veins. The glume ratio is more reliable for this pair than purple color or panicle openness.
shared_traits: True grasses with jointed culms, sheathing leaves and a hair-fringed ligule.
Each spikelet contains one fertile floret enclosed by two persistent glumes; the firm, narrow lemma bears three terminal awn branches.
Both species may have spreading or somewhat open panicles and long awns; three awns confirm the genus, not the species.
shared_genus_recognition.learning_sequence: whole clump and persistent basal foliage → isolated intact spikelet → lower versus upper glume lengths and lower-glume veins → lemma/awn anatomy → collar and sheath

look_here_first_sequence.target: Isolate one fertile floret and count three awns arising from ONE lemma, not three spikelets.
Lay lower and upper glumes side by side, exclude any terminal awn, and compare their lengths.
Backlight the lower glume at 10–20×: 1 prominent vein favors A. purpurea; 3–7 favors A. oligantha.
Perennial A. purpurea retains a persistent dense basal crown; annual A. oligantha often has wiry culms with more foliage/branching above base.
Compare spikelet body length and panicle architecture; do not identify from awn length, purple tint or panicle openness alone.

species_comparison_matrix.Aristida oligantha: Annual; no persistent perennial crown; wiry culms, commonly branching from base and nodes.

species_comparison_matrix.Aristida purpurea: Often narrow, nodding or flexuous; may be open or have spreading branches.
species_comparison_matrix.Aristida oligantha: Texas plants often have a sparse, openly branched, few-spikeleted panicle; descriptions vary by treatment.

species_comparison_matrix.Aristida purpurea: Mostly basal involute blades, roughly 0.7–2 mm wide; hairs conspicuous at collar in Texas treatment.
species_comparison_matrix.Aristida oligantha: Mostly cauline filiform blades, roughly 1–2 mm wide; ligule a hair fringe, collar hairs variable.

species_comparison_matrix.Aristida purpurea: Three long, spreading, near-equal awns; typical GrassBase limbs 35–45 mm, but A. purpurea varieties vary widely.
species_comparison_matrix.Aristida oligantha: Three long, spreading, near-equal awns; typical GrassBase limbs 30–70 mm.

overlap_cautions: Three long awns identify Aristida, not which of these two species is present.
Both panicles may be open. Existing field shorthand ('oligantha airy; purpurea narrow') is a supporting gestalt, not a dependable dichotomous key.
A. purpurea is variable across recognized varieties; glume/awn dimensions from broad species treatments should be checked against local vouchers if intermediate.
Glumes persist after floret dispersal; measure an intact spikelet or match the retained pair to the correct floret.
Purple coloration is seasonal and shared by both; do not use it to separate them.

Conflicting secondary descriptions of A. oligantha stamen number (Go Botany lists 1; Kew GrassBase lists 3) must not be taught as a separating character until Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review resolves the discrepancy.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.separator: Usually one lemma awn or no awn, not three arising from one hardened lemma; compare whole spikelet under magnification.
Typically one conspicuous lemma awn, not three equal branches; confirm glumes and lemma.
Often awnless small spikelets; lack Aristida's three-armed lemma awn.
Distinctive spikes or branches with multiple spikelets; do not mistake multiple awned spikelets for three awns on a single Aristida floret.

comparison_only.name: Aristida longespica
comparison_only.alias: Aristida longispica (frequent older spelling in UT Central Texas gallery)
comparison_only.source_presence: UT Austin's primarily NW Hays/Travis Central Texas grasses listing, not a three-county PASS
comparison_only.first_look: Look for relatively contracted, slender/spike-like panicle; SHORT glumes about 3–9 mm versus very long, spreading awns of A. oligantha, and distinctly shortened lateral awns versus the central awn.
comparison_only.awn: Central awn length highly variable by variety: var. geniculata often 12–27 mm (or longer in some Texas treatments), laterals often 6–18 mm; var. longespica central 1–10(14) mm, laterals 0–5(8) mm.
comparison_only.key_splits: Unlike A. dichotoma, the central awn is NOT spirally coiled at its base at maturity; unlike A. purpurea, plant is ANNUAL with lateral awns commonly significantly shorter than central.
comparison_only.caution: Multiple varieties and intermediates. UT page writes A. longispica, an orthographic variant of accepted A. longespica, not an extra species.

comparison_only.name: Aristida dichotoma
comparison_only.source_presence: Listed among grasses in UT Central Texas gallery (primarily NW Hays/Travis); county-level PASS not established by this reference
comparison_only.first_look: Start with VERY SHORT awns, particularly the central awn at maturity that is spirally COILED at the base rather than straight, and two shorter erect lateral awns.
comparison_only.awn: Typical central awn ~3–8 mm, coiled at base (roughly half turn to several turns); lateral awns 1–4 mm, straight/erect, markedly shorter than central.
comparison_only.key_splits: Unlike A. longespica, central awn base COILED. Unlike A. oligantha, awns tiny rather than 35–70 mm long and spreading; lower glume 1-veined rather than 3–7.
comparison_only.caution: Photographs of entire heads can obscure tiny curled awns. The structure must be photographed with a ruler/macro; some other Aristida (A. basiramea) also coil the central awn but have longer awns.

comparison_matrix.name: Aristida purpurea
comparison_matrix.panicle: Often narrow, can be somewhat open
comparison_matrix.lower_glume: Typically ~6–8 mm; shorter than upper ~11–15 mm, commonly 1 vein
comparison_matrix.awn: Three long spreading near-equal awns; often 35–45 mm in typical species description
comparison_matrix.priority: Persistent perennial crown + UNEQUAL glumes + one lower-glume vein; flower color not decisive

comparison_matrix.name: Aristida oligantha
comparison_matrix.lower_glume: Typically ~18–25 mm and ~equal to upper; 3–7 veins
comparison_matrix.awn: Three long near-equal widely spreading awns often 35–65(70) mm
comparison_matrix.priority: Long EQUAL glumes with 3–7 lower-glume veins; long widely spread awns

comparison_matrix.name: Aristida longespica
comparison_matrix.awn: Usually UNEQUAL: central typically 1–27 mm (varies by variety), lateral usually shorter up to ~18 mm; not spirally coiled at base
comparison_matrix.priority: NARROW panicle + relatively short glumes + SHORTER lateral awns; avoid wrong historical spelling

comparison_matrix.name: Aristida dichotoma
comparison_matrix.lower_glume: Usually 1-veined; glumes typically shorter than oligantha
comparison_matrix.awn: Very SHORT central ~3–8 mm, basal COIL; lateral ~1–4 mm, erect
comparison_matrix.priority: Tiny awn triplet, central coiled at base. Macro required for confident call

decision_sequence: 1. Confirm three awns from ONE lemma; if there are three awned spikelets, not three awns on one floret, re-check genus.
2. Are THREE awns very long (~35–70 mm), spread widely AND lower glume 3–7-veined? → A. oligantha.
3. Are awns VERY short, with central tip ~3–8 mm coiled at base and erect side tips ~1–4 mm? → A. dichotoma, COMPARISON ONLY.
4. Annual + narrow contracted panicle, short glumes ~3–9 mm, lateral awns shorter than uncoiled central? → A. longespica, COMPARISON ONLY (variety affects awn lengths).
5. Persistent densely rooted PERENNIAL bunch, long subequal awns, lower glume shorter than upper and typically single-veined? → A. purpurea.
6. If intermediate or characters contradictory, label Aristida sp.; check FNA/Texas flora and local voucher before forcing a species.
